content.title: Dhurandhar The Revenge (2026) ⭐ 8.7 | Action, Crime, Thriller
content.text: Videos3Featured reviewsDelivers Exactly What It PromisesWalking into Dhurandhar 2 with high expectations and long-built anticipation, I got to experience it exactly the way I had hoped to, and once again, keeping all socio-politics and the obvious, expected talks of propaganda aside, purely from a cinematic storytelling perspective, it delivers, and how.It starts off with the origin tale, spending enough time to keep you invested in the story, before seamlessly transitioning back to the political conflicts of the first part.The use of classic music and sound design remains on point yet again, especially during the high-octane, gory action. Captured beautifully, it delivers just the right amount of mass needed. Beyond the performances, this is what truly stands out as the film's biggest strength.Needless to say, Ranveer Singh is a beast and the epitome of the ideal massy hero in this one, but he delivers equally well in the emotional moments too. A special mention to Arjun Rampal for carrying out his menacing side so effortlessly.The screenplay feels well-balanced, giving each character their moments to shine, with sprinkles of comedic writing that further balance its otherwise bloody tone.With multiple fast-paced twists and montages in the second half, the narrative takes an interesting turn, building up to a slightly long yet gripping climax, with a few cliché one-liners often heard in films following the patriotic template.For someone who walked in with expectations, I would say it has several moments where it exceeds itself and goes beyond them.Those who walk in with a clear, open mind are sure to be met with plenty of surprises, keeping them on the edge of their seats until the very end.All in all, given the hype and excitement surrounding it since the first part, one can easily bet that this is a film with the potential to enjoy a long theatrical run and even break records. So if you are interested, do yourself a favour and watch it on the big screen.It is sure to elevate the experience in ways one cannot imagine.Epic Revenge DeliveredHonestly, a wonderful and satisfying sequel! Ranveer Singh is on a different level, delivering raw intensity, emotion, and layers that hit hard. Easily one of his best performances. Although I loved the first part more and Akshaye Khanna was excellent, here I didn't miss him for even a minute thanks to Ranveer's amazing performance. Aditya Dhar's direction is impressive with mind-boggling twists, high-octane action, and an emotional punch that will leave you emotional at points. I'm really impressed with how the writers have connected real-life events with the story. Casting director Mukesh Chhabra hits sixer. National award should introduce best Casting director award just for him. Music was good but according to some people it's not as good as first part. I tell you this soundtrack is a slow poison. Some songs are even better than first soundtrack.Film is nearly 4-hour but runtime flies by thanks to the solid pacing and epic sequence. However, the long-ass fight in Chapter 6 could have shorter. I feel Jaskirat Singh Rangi's original story should have been given more time! It got half an hour, but it still needed more. Anyways you can say they could have avoided some dialogues regarding government still, it's a colossal, satisfying sequel that lives up to the insane hype.A New Day Has ComeI really enjoyed the first part of Dhurandhar and ended my review expecting Part 2 to unleash the real action, bring forth the true evil of some of the characters, provide a peek into the protagonist's troubled past, reveal a big character, take the tension to the next level and descend into real chaos. So did Dhurandhar: The Revenge meet my expectations? - It simply blew the lid off all my expectations.Dhurandhar: The Revenge is grittier, gorier and greater than the first chapter of the saga as it does a great job in completing the story arcs of all its characters. The movie starts with an adrenaline infused, blood soaked and expletive laden chapter diving into the back story of the movie's protagonist Jaskirat Singh Rangi. There is more blood, guts and violence in this one chapter than almost the entire first part of the saga. This chapter sets the tone of the movie....expect to see a huge splattering of blood, a barrage of chopped body parts and a flurry of offensive curse words over its nearly 4 hour run time. And just like this first chapter, the movie gets to the point without wasting any time.Even at 229 minutes, The Revenge is highly gripping and thorougly entertaining with great performance by the entire cast. The brightest of them all is Ranveer Singh who as Jaskirat and Hamza gives two very different superlative performances. Jaskirat's eyes ooze fire, emotions and melancholy while Hamza channels anger, confidence and resolve. Madhavan looks even more like his real life character than the first part and has some fantastic moments in the movie. If you liked Rakesh Bedi's performance in the first part, then this time around you will applaud and give him a very deserving standing ovation.Sanjay Dutt manages to elevate his performance in the 2nd part as compared to the first movie and delivers some really punchy moments throughout the movie. Arjun Rampal doesnt fully rise to the level that I had hoped for as the lead antagonist of this part but still does a good job. His side story with a really revolting and foul mouth father feels a bit distracting but is still well executed. The Bade Sahab storyline is pretty good even though it doesnt fill the gargantuan gap created by the absent Rehman Dacait who completely raised the level of the first part. Uzair Baloch and Yalina fade to the background in this part but are still effective in their respective scenes. The movie doesnt waste any time introducing a handful of new characters. As a result Aditya Dhar creates a second part of the saga which is unexpected and different than most fan theories, making the movie very interesting and engaging.The inspired and very well re-imagined background music and soundtrack are terrific. The realistic sets, action sequences, explosions are all very well executed. Dhurandhar is inspired from real characters and real life events but at the end of the day it is still a work of fiction. Hence even though there are some clear elements of propaganda and bias, it is not an outright propaganda movie....it is an entertaining movie and should be watched, reviewed and enjoyed as a fictional movie and not a real life documentary.Aditya Dhar has done a phenomenal job creating a realistic spy universe and filled it with characters that audiences will both love and hate with equal intensity. We feel the pain, melancholy, anxiety, helplessness, courage and patriotism of these characters and also sense the evil, hate and viciousness that confronts them. Kudos to him and the entire cast and crew for not only managing to create a movie that not only reaches but even manages to exceed the level and quality of the first part.If you liked the first part then you will definitely enjoy The Revenge. If Dhurandhar was not your cup of tea because of its violence, gore and expletiveness then its conclusion is not only more of the same but the brutality, hyperviolence and profanity dialed up to near maximum. Overall the movie is extremely gripping, very well made with brilliant performances and extremely good direction. It is very long but not boring at all. It is not an easy watch but a must watch in cinema for those who liked the first part. I loved it. Records will be broken. A New Day has Come. 9/10.ANOTHER Blockbuster#DhurandharTheRevenge - PEAK.. Once again, huge shout out to Shashwat Sachdev, he should be used more in Hindi cinema, could be the next AR Rahman Name any genre, his score has all of it.PhenomenalI don't like action or political movies because I don't believe war or hatred of another nation is healthy. But this movie is phenomenal leaving all the politics and whatever propaganda aside. Ranveer Singh did a phenomenal job, he deserves every single award ever for his role. He worked so hard, he shines like a diamond in this movie. The second actor that stood out to me was Arjun Rampal- what a class actor. He deserves more roles and films. Aditya Dhar is an amazing director, the story did not feel extensive even if it was four hours long. My only gripe is there were too many swear words that were not necessary at all.
